comparablySuitable.definition: Two candidates are comparably suitable when they have the same source-support level and the same suitability band (band 0: at most 2 'concern' criteria; band 1: 3 or more). Only then does tradition preference decide.

combined.rule: All eligible records of either tradition compete under selectionOrder. A Western record is used where it gives suitable additional coverage (its complementsIndianGap states why no comparably suitable Indian reading exists for that feature). No tradition quota, slot or ratio.

indian-only.rule: Only Indian records. A category with no Indian record is listed as not assessed with reason 'no-supported-content'. Western content is never substituted and no Indian equivalent is generated.

western-only.rule: Only Western records. Excluded Western meanings (life line as lifespan, fate line as destiny, marriage/children lines, health) stay excluded. Cross-tradition conflict notes (e.g. the āyurlekhā note) are still shown because they are safety disclosures, not interpretations.

placement.description: Candidates are ranked by selectionOrder (comparablySuitable decides when tradition preference applies). In rank order, each item goes into the first category in its own 'categories' list that has fewer than maxInterpretationsPerCategory items; an item with no room goes under 'More from your reading'. An item appears once. Within a section, items are shown in rank order.

tierFrames.tentative: Shown as tradition-attributed text with the note: 'This is what a palm-reading tradition said, not a finding about you.'
tierFrames.clear: NOT USED: owner decision C1-D3 (2026-11-24) sets tentative as the ceiling for every record, including automatic measurements.

globalPolicy.thresholdNote: All numeric ranges are placeholders. None is source-defined; the sources give qualitative descriptions only. E1 must calibrate on synthetic data and the reviewer must accept that no threshold carries traditional authority.

observation.descriptor: presence of a confirmed trace

sources.note: Editor's variant reading also names the line 'knowledge'.

interpretations.traditionalInterpretation: An early Buddhist palmistry chapter (after the mid-9th c.) describes a second line rising from the base of the thumb as existing 'for the sake of knowledge'; later Indian hand diagrams label the line the father's line, and one names it after Sarasvatī, goddess of learning. The texts do not say how the line's shape changes the reading.

userFacing.observation: You traced the line that curves from the base of your thumb.
userFacing.reading: In Indian palm-reading tradition this is the pitṛlekhā, which an early text calls a line of knowledge, and which later diagrams link with Sarasvatī, the goddess of learning.
userFacing.reflection: What are you learning at the moment purely because it interests you?
userFacing.applicationNote: The texts name this line after knowledge for everyone who has it; tracing it does not say anything about how much you know. The reflection is Aura's, not the text's.
